clue.text: Piscator's round

definitions.meaning: a piscator is an angler, and what an angler lands is his haul of fish
a round is a song for several voices entering in turn, like a glee

explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both senses: an angler's haul of fish, and a part-song sung in canon.

clue.text: New boiler put in Tom's one-horse shay

indicators.note: put in tells us the shuffled letters go inside the word for a tom

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

indicators.note: new signals the letters of boiler made afresh into another order

explanation.surface: A fresh boiler is fitted into Tom's little horse-drawn carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' is a tomcat, not a man's name. 'New' signals the anagram BRIOLE, and 'put in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A light two-wheeled carriage drawn by a single horse is the classic example of a shay.

clue.text: In France you intimate a length (of this material ?) to take up

parts.note: tu is the familiar, intimate French word for you

indicators.note: in a down clue, taking up means the word for a length is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: an ell is an old measure of length, used for cloth

explanation.surface: A Frenchman addresses someone familiarly while measuring out cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take up' reverses ELL to give LLE in this down entry; 'this material' points at the fabric being measured.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulle is a fine silk or net fabric, the material of veils and tutus.

clue.text: They can store many a bottle safely

definitions.text: They can store many a bottle safely

parts.words: They can store many a bottle safely
parts.note: a bottle here is a bundle of hay, not a wine bottle, so these are stacks holding bundles of fodder

explanation.definitionFit: Stacks of hay in a field hold many bundles of dried grass, once called bottles.

clue.text: Is this what drowses the pew-sitters?

definitions.text: Is this what drowses the pew-sitters?

parts.words: Is this what drowses the pew-sitters?
parts.note: a carved finial on the end of a church pew bears the name of the sleep-inducing flower's seed pod

explanation.walkthrough: The carved ornament topping a pew end shares its name with the seed head of the opium flower, which brings sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: The carved finial on a church bench end is named after the seed capsule of the opium flower.

clue.text: Professor, 'Scots one, and irreverent

parts.note: ane is the Scots word for one

explanation.surface: A Scottish professor is described as disrespectful.
explanation.definitionFit: Profane speech or behaviour shows contempt for sacred things, the opposite of reverence.

clue.text: Water bearer has a sporting fling

definitions.meaning: a jug for carrying and pouring water
in baseball the player who throws the ball has a fling at the batter

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: a large jug for water, and the baseball player who hurls the ball.

clue.text: There was gold over there, round our country

indicators.note: round says the word for over there goes around the abbreviation for our country

parts.note: yon is an old word meaning over there
UK, the United Kingdom, is the setter's country

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a place far off where gold was found, compared with home.
explanation.walkthrough: The Klondike gold rush of the 1890s took place in this Canadian territory.
explanation.definitionFit: This north-western Canadian territory was the scene of the Klondike gold rush.

clue.text: Filling out with a "big big D—"

definitions.meaning: as a grammar term, a word serving only to fill out a sentence or verse line
a swear word, from the 'big, big D' (damn) of Gilbert and Sullivan's HMS Pinafore

explanation.walkthrough: In HMS Pinafore the captain lets slip a 'big, big D', meaning damn.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a padding word in a sentence and an oath or curse.

clue.text: " Where is it now, the glory and the" (Wordsworth)

definitions.text: Where is it now, the glory and the

parts.words: Where is it now, the glory and the
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from the closing line of a stanza of Wordsworth's ode on Intimations of Immortality

explanation.definitionFit: Wordsworth's ode laments the lost visionary gleam of childhood, the glory and the vision of sleep.

clue.text: Bearded male wears toga capriciously

annotationWithheld.why: Bearded male wears toga capriciously (5-4): GOAT is an anagram of toga, but nothing in the clue as printed (scan agrees) supplies BILLY

clue.text: African hill where the jay is not heard

definitions.text: African hill where the jay is not heard

parts.words: African hill where the jay is not heard
parts.note: a small South African hill whose Afrikaans name is spelt with a J that is pronounced like Y, so the letter jay is silent

explanation.walkthrough: The jay is the letter J, not the bird: the Afrikaans word is spoken 'koppie'.
explanation.definitionFit: In South Africa a small isolated hill on the veld is known by this Afrikaans word.

clue.text: Sluggish mutation of nitre

indicators.note: a mutation is a change, so the letters of nitre are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Nitre is a sluggish chemical in some altered form.
explanation.definitionFit: Inert means inactive or slow to move, like a chemically unreactive substance.

clue.text: Goddess maimed emu with a club

parts.note: Athena is the Greek goddess of wisdom

indicators.note: maimed means damaged, so the letters of emu are broken into a new order

explanation.surface: A goddess injures a flightless bird with a cudgel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the pieces; 'club' looks like a weapon but is a gentlemen's club, the London Athenaeum.
explanation.definitionFit: The Athenaeum is a famous London gentlemen's club, and the name is used generally for literary clubs.

clue.text: Old physician has nil return with land unit

indicators.note: a return is a turning back, so the word nil is read backwards

parts.note: an acre is a unit of land area

explanation.surface: An old doctor has made no return on his patch of land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns NIL into LIN. Thomas Linacre was physician to Henry VIII and founded the Royal College of Physicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Linacre was a Tudor doctor who founded the Royal College of Physicians.

clue.text: Professional publicity bold as brass

parts.note: the brass plate by a doctor's or lawyer's door advertises the practice, literally made of brass

explanation.definitionFit: A brass plaque outside an office announces the occupant's profession to passers-by.

clue.text: Electricity breaking circuit gone out of control

indicators.note: breaking means the word for electricity bursts into the word for a circuit

parts.note: a ring is a circuit, a closed loop
amp, the ampere, is the unit of electric current

explanation.surface: A power surge breaks into a circuit and things run wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' is the container signal; 'circuit' looks electrical alongside 'Electricity' but is just a ring. The page prints no '19'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramping means rampaging or storming about wildly, behaving without restraint.

clue.text: Such tombs broken, alarm Rome

indicators.note: broken signals the letters of alarm Rome smashed and rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: Tombs are smashed, causing alarm in Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmoreal means made of or like marble, the stone of grand monuments.

clue.text: Green light to wizard newsman hot perhaps

parts.note: go is what a green traffic light signals
a wizard casts spells, so he is jokingly a speller

explanation.surface: A reporter, perhaps a hot one, is given clearance by a magician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' joins the pieces; the newsman spreads the gospel, the good news, and a 'hot gospeller' is a fervent evangelist.
explanation.definitionFit: A preacher of the Gospel spreads good tidings, and a fervent one is called a 'hot' one.

clue.text: Docile sister who may have helped the Romans to barge in

definitions.text: who may have helped the Romans to barge in

parts.note: docile means tame

explanation.surface: A meek sister may have helped invading Romans force their way in.
explanation.walkthrough: Tamesis was the Roman name for the Thames, a river carrying barges; 'barge in' looks like intruding.
explanation.definitionFit: The Romans called London's great river by this Latin name, and floated barges on it.

clue.text: Rebecca has directions to improve her wit

parts.note: Rebecca (Becky) Sharp is the scheming heroine of Thackeray's Vanity Fair
E (east) is a compass direction
N (north) is a compass direction

explanation.surface: Becky is given instructions to become more witty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' joins the pieces. Becky Sharp, a famously quick-witted heroine, makes the wit apt.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a wit keener is to hone it, as a blade is given a finer edge.

clue.text: Little tooters ? Painfully sharp

definitions.meaning: small horns, with the diminutive ending -et added to the instrument
large wasps with a painful sting

explanation.definitionFit: The word can be read as small horns, and is also the name of big stinging wasps.

clue.text: Cabins for Elian Margatebound Audreys?

parts.note: Elia (Charles Lamb) wrote the essay The Old Margate Hoy, a hoy being a small coasting boat
dens are small private rooms or cabins

explanation.surface: Cabins on a boat bound for the seaside are set aside for country girls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' joins the pieces; Margate is a Kent seaside resort. Audrey is the rustic wench in As You Like It, so 'Audreys' are boisterous girls.
explanation.definitionFit: Audrey, Shakespeare's country lass, typifies the boisterous, rough-mannered girl.

clue.text: Distance lent enchantment to its, view for Tommy

definitions.text: Distance lent enchantment to its, view for Tommy

parts.words: Distance lent enchantment to its, view for Tommy
parts.note: the British soldier's marching song says it is a long way to this Irish town, so distance made it romantic

explanation.walkthrough: Tommy (Tommy Atkins) is the British private soldier; the WW1 song is 'It's a Long Way to ...'. 'Distance lends enchantment to the view' is a proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish town is the far-off destination of the famous First World War marching song.

clue.text: Alexander's girl-friend saith otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means in a different way, so the letters of saith are arranged differently

explanation.definitionFit: The Athenian courtesan was the companion of Alexander the Great, celebrated in Dryden's ode.

clue.text: What's behind the becomingly picturesque ?

parts.note: a picture in the making, one becoming a picture, stands propped on a painter's wooden frame

explanation.definitionFit: A painter's stand holds the canvas upright while the picture is being made.

clue.text: Stony-hearted girl

definitions.meaning: a small fruit with a hard stone at its centre

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a stone fruit of the Mediterranean, and is also a girl's name.

clue.text: I eat late, say, and get frozen

indicators.note: say signals that the words for I eat late are spoken and heard as the answer

parts.note: to sup is to eat a late supper, so I eat late is I sup

explanation.surface: Someone who dines late finds the food gone cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I sup', spoken quickly, sounds like the phrasal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To ice up is to become coated with or blocked by frost.

clue.text: Parent backs Titania's Love to make a packet

indicators.note: backs here means goes backwards, so the word for parent is read in reverse

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
in A Midsummer Night's Dream the fairy queen falls for Bottom wearing a donkey's head

explanation.surface: A mother supports the fairy queen's sweetheart so as to earn a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs' reverses MA into AM. 'make a packet' is British slang for earning a lot of money.
explanation.definitionFit: To pile up wealth is to gather it together, as one who makes a packet does.

clue.text: How Eric dined ?

parts.note: Farrar's school story is Eric, or, Little by Little, so Eric would have eaten a little at a time

explanation.walkthrough: Dean Farrar's Victorian school novel is subtitled 'Little by Little'; read as 'piece meal' it is a meal in bits.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something bit by bit, a little at a time, matches the novel's subtitle.

clue.text: In fun-fair attractions "e'll get these bumps

indicators.note: in places the cockney contraction inside the word for fun-fair rides

parts.note: swings are rides at a fair
e'll is he'll with the h dropped, as a cockney would say it

explanation.surface: A fairground visitor is warned that the rides will leave him bruised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is the container signal; the apostrophe in 'e'll marks a dropped H, a Cockney touch that fits the fairground.
explanation.definitionFit: Swellings are raised lumps on the skin, the result of knocks.

clue.text: Takes a common girl to speed his gait

annotationWithheld.why: Takes a common girl to speed his gait (5): LOPER is one who lopes, but no parse of 'Takes a common girl' gives the letters; the scan agrees with the held text
